cards.name: Solarize
cards.summary: Blends a negative and a positive of the image, like briefly exposing a photo print to light in the darkroom: tones above mid-grey are inverted, tones below stay, so highlights turn dark and the whole image drops to a dim, low-contrast, slightly psychedelic version with no bright values left. No dialog and no settings.
use_for: retro darkroom / solarised portrait look for a poster
psychedelic or surreal album-cover and gig artwork
a quick dark, eerie variant of a photo to sit behind light type
avoid: on its own the result is muddy (nothing brighter than mid-grey): follow with Image/Adjustments/Levels or Image/Auto Contrast to stretch it back
you need control over where the inversion starts: use a Curves adjustment layer with an inverted-V curve instead, which is also editable
Lab documents: not supported (harvest supported_modes: RGB, CMYK, Grayscale, Duotone, Multichannel); in CMYK each ink channel is inverted separately, so colours shift differently than in RGB
pairs_with: Image/Adjustments/Levels or Image/Auto Contrast right after, to restore brightness
Image/Adjustments/Hue/Saturation to colour-tint the result
Filter/Convert for Smart Filters so it can be toggled
cards.scripting: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("solarize"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO);  // no parameters; runs on the active pixel layer
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer (it rewrites the pixels); on a Smart Object it becomes a removable Smart Filter: the harvest's smart-filter probe (work/ps/probe_smart.json (a local file, not shipped), smart_filter true in harvest/ps/ps_filter.json) applied it to a Smart Object and read it back as a Smart Filter entry with no settings to reopen (hasoptions false), only its blending options (opacity, mode)

verified.note: Dim, low-contrast psychedelic frame: highlights inverted to dark, the grey ramp runs black-grey-black, no bright values left.

cards.name: Tiles
cards.summary: Cuts the image into a grid of square tiles and nudges each tile off its original position by a random amount, leaving gaps between them filled with the Background colour, the Foreground colour, an inverted copy of the image or the unaltered image; the result looks like a photo printed on shuffled ceramic tiles or a broken-up puzzle.
use_for: broken / shattered-grid treatment of a photo for a tech or glitch poster
tiled-wall or puzzle look behind a headline
a quick fragmented background texture from any photo
avoid: fine control of tile placement: the offsets are random, so a rerun gives a different layout
Fill Empty With Background / Foreground depends on the current swatches: set them first, or use Inverse Image / Unaltered Image for a swatch-independent result
an even pixel-block look without gaps: use Filter/Pixelate/Mosaic instead

params.name: Number Of Tiles
params.does: minimum number of tiles in each row and column, so higher = smaller tiles
params.typical: 1-99; 10 default, 8-16 on a full HD image

params.name: Maximum Offset
params.does: how far a tile may move from its place, as a percent of the tile size; higher = wider gaps and a more broken look
params.typical: 1-99; 10 default, 20-40 for a clearly shattered look

params.name: Fill Empty With
params.does: what shows in the gaps between tiles: Background colour, Foreground colour, Inverse Image (a negative) or Unaltered Image (the original peeks through)
params.typical: Background Color for clean grout in the swatch colour; Inverse Image for a graphic, colourful look

pairs_with: set the Background swatch to the grout colour you want first
Layer Style Drop Shadow / Bevel on a duplicate for raised tiles
Filter/Convert for Smart Filters

cards.name: Trace Contour
cards.summary: Finds where brightness crosses a chosen level and draws a thin outline there in each colour channel, wiping everything else to white: the photo becomes a sparse topographic-map drawing of thin coloured contour lines on white.
use_for: contour-map / topographic line art from a photo for a poster background
thin-line technical-drawing look from a photo
a starting outline to colour or trace over
avoid: scripts trusting a Level value: the harvest read no range; sending +/-1e6 left Level at 128 (inconclusive, the value was apparently refused rather than clamped), so read 'level' back from the descriptor executeAction returns, or from the Smart Filter, to confirm it was used
soft or low-contrast photos give few, broken lines: raise contrast first, or move Level to the tone where the subject edge sits
clean black outlines: in RGB the lines come out in mixed channel colours; desaturate afterwards, or use Filter/Stylize/Find Edges for darker, fuller edges

params.name: Level
params.does: brightness threshold whose crossing is outlined; moves the lines between shadow and highlight regions
params.typical: 128 (the value the harvest saw); move it toward the tone where the subject's edge sits

params.name: Edge
params.does: which side of the threshold is outlined: lower = where values fall below Level, upper = where they rise above it
params.typical: upper or lower; small visual difference

pairs_with: Image/Adjustments/Desaturate or Threshold for single-colour line art
Layer blend mode Multiply over the original photo
Image/Adjustments/Levels first to boost contrast

cards.name: Wind
cards.summary: Draws fine horizontal streaks out of the edges and bright areas of the image, as if the picture were being blown sideways: Wind gives short thin streaks, Blast longer and stronger ones, Stagger shifts the streaked lines out of register.
use_for: speed / motion streaks on a product, car or sports headline

avoid: it only blows horizontally: for vertical streaks rotate the canvas 90 degrees (Image/Image Rotation), apply, rotate back
a soft blur-like motion: use Filter/Blur/Motion Blur; Wind makes hard, hairline streaks

which way the streaks run for each Direction value was not checked by the harvest: preview once before a batch run

params.typical: Wind for subtle, Blast for a clear effect

params.name: Direction
params.does: which side the wind blows from (the dialog's From the Left / From the Right)
params.typical: Left or Right; match the motion of the subject
